item.title: Gram–Schmidt Process and QR
item.description:
The Gram–Schmidt process turns any basis into an orthonormal basis; it is the constructive step behind the QR factorization and many orthogonalization methods.

Algorithm

Given a basis ${\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_n}$:

Step 1 – Orthogonalize:

  1. $\mathbf{u}_1 = \mathbf{v}_1$
  2. $\mathbf{u}_2 = \mathbf{v}2 - \text{proj}{\mathbf{u}_1}(\mathbf{v}_2) = \mathbf{v}_2 - \frac{\langle \mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{u}_1 \rangle}{\langle \mathbf{u}_1, \mathbf{u}_1 \rangle} \mathbf{u}_1$
  3. $\mathbf{u}_k = \mathbf{v}k - \sum{j=1}^{k-1} \frac{\langle \mathbf{v}_k, \mathbf{u}_j \rangle}{\langle \mathbf{u}_j, \mathbf{u}_j \rangle} \mathbf{u}_j$

Step 2 – Normalize: $\mathbf{e}_i = \mathbf{u}_i / |\mathbf{u}_i|$.
